Senator, the real issue is the OBBBA’s structural failures. Your provision’s removal highlights the bill’s core flaw: D.C. prioritizes political theater over real reform. The original legislation already fell $4.4 trillion short of pre-pandemic fiscal baselines while embedding loopholes for special interests.

Medicaid needs targeted fixes—like ending pharma overpayments and consultant bloat—not temporary cash infusions. The parliamentarian’s ruling proves this bill was never about sustainable solutions.

Alaska’s health crisis demands permanent restructuring, not another D.C. shell game where “increased funding” vanishes faster than a bureaucrat’s accountability.

Senate Democrats also successfully stripped my provision from the budget reconciliation bill addressing major cost disparities for Alaska’s many rural hospitals—more Senate Democrat hypocrisy on health care in Alaska. But we will keep fighting for Alaska’s rural hospitals!

Unfortunately, this is part of the Senate Democrats’ continuing assault on so many of the positive provisions for Alaska in the budget reconciliation bill. The following provisions—that we are fighting to keep in the final bill—have all been fought by Chuck Schumer and Senate Democrats to strip out of the bill:

➡️ ANWR leases
➡️ NPR-A leases
➡️ Cook Inlet leases
➡️ Coast Guard funding for Alaska, including facilities for the new icebreaker home-ported in Juneau
➡️ Potential Arctic military bases
➡️ Border security
